title: zig build test-env-verify / test-wiring-check fail on Windows when python3 resolves to the WindowsApps App Execution Alias stub
scope: build.zig verification steps only (test-env-verify, test-wiring-check). No effect on the underlying scripts' correctness.
symptom: On a Windows machine where python3.exe resolves to the WindowsApps App Execution Alias stub before a real interpreter, `zig build test-env-verify` and `zig build test-wiring-check` fail immediately with 'Python was not found ... error code 49', even though the underlying scripts are correct and run fine via `python tools/verify_test_env.py` / `python tools/lint_test_wiring.py` directly.
reproduction: On a Windows machine with a broken python3 App Execution Alias ahead of a working interpreter on PATH: zig build test-env-verify (or test-wiring-check)
root_cause_analysis: build.zig's addSystemCommand for these two steps hardcodes "python3" as the executable name. Every other Python-invoking step in build.zig (lint_test_table_refs, clean_test_db) uses "python" instead. On this dev machine, python3 has two resolutions on PATH: the broken WindowsApps stub (first) and a working AppData\Local\Python\bin\python3.exe (second) -- the stub wins.
acceptance_criteria: zig build test-env-verify succeeds on a Windows machine with an unresolved python3 App Execution Alias stub, assuming underlying infra is healthy
zig build test-wiring-check succeeds under the same condition
No change to either script's detection logic -- interpreter selection only
evidence_file: GH #440 has full reproduction and suggested fix (switch to "python" for consistency with existing build.zig convention)
